Px4FlightModesConfig.assignAPx4FlightModeTo: Assign a PX4 flight mode to each of the 6 positions of your mode switch. PX4 splits the chosen RC channel into 6 equal ranges (slot 1 lowest, slot 6 highest) and applies the mode whose range the channel lands in. Unassigned slots are skipped.
Px4FlightModesConfig.whichRcChannelSelectsTheFlight: Which RC channel selects the flight mode
Px4FlightModesConfig.noChannelAssignedSelectTheChannel: No channel assigned. Select the channel wired to your mode switch.
Px4FlightModesConfig.connectToTheVehicleAndMove: Connect to the vehicle and move your mode switch to see the active slot highlighted live.

Px4ReceiverConfig.px4CanTakeManualControlFrom: PX4 can take manual control from an RC receiver, a ground-station joystick, or both. Choose the source that matches your setup. Most pilots use RC only. The RC loss timeout (COM_RC_LOSS_T) and failsafe action live in the Safety tab.

Px4ReceiverConfig.perChannelEndpointsCenterDeadzoneAnd: Per-channel endpoints, center, deadzone and reverse

Move each stick to its extremes and read the live values above, then enter Min, Max and Trim (center) here. Deadzone ignores small jitter around center. Reverse flips a channel direction.

RoverTuningTab.ardupilotStockFullPowerNoSoftening: ArduPilot stock: full power, no softening
RoverTuningTab.softAroundCentreFullLockUnchanged: Soft around centre, full lock unchanged
RoverTuningTab.theseSettingsControlHowYourRover: These settings control how your rover follows waypoints and holds position. L1 controller determines path following accuracy - lower period = tighter turns but more oscillation.
RoverTuningTab.startWithDefaultL1SettingsAnd: Start with default L1 settings and only adjust if the rover oscillates on straight paths or cuts corners too much. Increase L1 Period for smoother driving, decrease for tighter following.
RoverTuningTab.configureHowFastYourRoverDrives: Configure how fast your rover drives and how it turns. Cruise speed is used for autonomous missions, max speed is the absolute limit.
RoverTuningTab.baseThrottlePercentageInAutoModes: Base throttle percentage in auto modes
RoverTuningTab.howTheRoverAnswersTheStick: How the rover answers the stick. The first three work in every mode including Manual; the acceleration limits only apply where the autopilot holds a speed.
RoverTuningTab.inTheStickIsTheMotor: In {{flightMode}} the stick is the motor output: what you set here is what you feel.
RoverTuningTab.inTheStickAsksForA: In {{flightMode}} the stick asks for a speed and a turn rate, and the controllers decide the outputs. Response depends on the steering and speed PIDs, not on these settings. Switch to Manual to feel the settings on this page directly.
RoverTuningTab.startFromOneOfTheseThen: Start from one of these, then fine-tune below. The chart follows every change.
RoverTuningTab.curveTopAccelLimitMS: Curve {{expo}}, top {{thrMax}}%, accel limit {{accel}} m/s². Leaves the throttle ramp alone.
RoverTuningTab.noLimitTheMotorsFollowThe: No limit: the motors follow the stick instantly. Leave it here unless the drivetrain needs protecting from sudden reversals.
RoverTuningTab.sFromStopToFullAnd: {{v1}} s from stop to full, and the same back: you will feel this as delay on the stick
RoverTuningTab.sFromStopToFullThrottle: {{v1}} s from stop to full throttle
RoverTuningTab.mostThrottleTheRoverWillEver: Most throttle the rover will ever use (%)
RoverTuningTab.softLowEndHalfStickGives: Soft low end: half stick gives well under half power
RoverTuningTab.strongLowEndForAMotor: Strong low end, for a motor that needs throttle before it pulls
RoverTuningTab.autoAndSpeedControlledModesOnly: Auto and speed-controlled modes only, m/s² (0 = no limit)
RoverTuningTab.howHardItMaySlowDown: How hard it may slow down, m/s² (0 = same as acceleration)
RoverTuningTab.mostRoverEscsCanDriveThe: Most rover ESCs can drive the motors backwards to slow the vehicle. ArduPilot only does it when told it may, and only in the modes where it controls speed: Acro, Steering, Auto and Guided. In Manual the stick IS the output, so pulling back commands reverse directly and what happens then is the ESC's own brake or reverse behaviour, not this setting.
RoverTuningTab.reversedOutputIsUsedToSlow: Reversed output is used to slow down; needs an ESC that can reverse
RoverTuningTab.theVehicleCoastsToAStop: The vehicle coasts to a stop instead
RoverTuningTab.outputsDropToZeroUnderThis: Outputs drop to zero under this speed (m/s), so it settles instead of hunting
RoverTuningTab.steeringHasItsOwnCurveAnd: Steering has its own curve, and it only shapes the stick in Manual. In Acro the stick asks for a turn rate instead.
RoverTuningTab.fullStickPutsServoAtTravel: Full stick puts servo {{ch}} at {{v2}}% travel ({{v3}}–{{v4}} µs)
RoverTuningTab.n100IsTheFull500S: 100% is the full ±500 µs a servo accepts. This scales the whole range rather than clipping it: at 40%, full stick gives 40% and half stick gives 20%. Turn it down when the wheels reach full lock before the stick does, so the travel you have left is travel that still steers.
RoverTuningTab.sSoItSteersFurtherOne: µs), so it steers further one way than the other. Moving the slider evens them up.
RoverTuningTab.calmAroundCentreFullLockStill: Calm around centre, full lock still reaches full lock
RoverTuningTab.sharperAroundCentreTwitchyRarelyWhat: Sharper around centre: twitchy, rarely what you want on a car
RoverTuningTab.linearStickAngleIsSteeringAngle: Linear: stick angle is steering angle
RoverTuningTab.minimumTurnRadiusAtLowSpeeds: Minimum turn radius at low speeds (m)
RoverTuningTab.aFullTurnTakesSAt: A full turn takes {{v1}} s at full lock
RoverTuningTab.forDifferentialDriveRoversThatCan: For differential drive rovers that can spin in place.
RoverTuningTab.angleToTargetBeforeUsingPivot: Angle to target before using pivot turn (0 = disabled)
RoverTuningTab.startWithConservativeSpeeds25: Start with conservative speeds (2-5 m/s) and increase gradually after testing. If your rover has skid steering (tank drive), enable pivot turns for sharper maneuvering.
